title: KV-cache interaction with FP8/INT8: tail-latency and throughput sweeping across batching/window settings
creator: Maya Chen
description: Objective: Produce a reproducible benchmark matrix that isolates how quantized model variants (FP8 E4M3, FP8 E5M2, INT8 symmetric per-channel) affect throughput, p50/p95/p99 latency and tail behavior when the attention KV cache is exercised under varying batching policies and long-context workloads. This ticket covers experiment design, harness implementation, runs on A100/H100, analysis of sources of tail latency (cold KV cache, dynamic kernel selection, batching window), and a short list of follow-ups (improved calibration, kernel hints).
acceptance_criteria:
1) End-to-end benchmark harness that runs automated sweeps across quant profiles, batching window (10/25/50/100ms), batch sizes (1/2/4/8), and sequence lengths (2k, 8k, 16k, 32k).
2) Collected p50/p95/p99 and throughput (tokens/sec) for each cell, with warm vs cold KV-cache delineation.
3) Calibration artifacts and the calibration configs used for each quant profile saved to GCS and linked in the run metadata.
4) Findings summarized in a perf memo with clear recommendations: when FP8/INT8 is acceptable (accuracy/regression thresholds), and batching windows that best balance tail latency vs throughput.
5) No regression >1.2% on eval accuracy (perplexity + MRR on retrieval subset) for approved profiles, or explicit rollback plan documented.
benchmark_plan:
- Hardware: H100 (8x) and A100 (4x), single-GPU primary measurements with multi-GPU throughput runs for scale validation.
- Models: base 7B and 70B architecture variants (same model family) converted to FP8 (E4M3 & E5M2) and INT8 (per-channel symmetric with KL and histogram calibration).
- Calibration: compare per-layer minmax, percentile (99.999), and KL divergence calibration using a curated 10k token representative dataset (web+docs mix). Store calibration tables and quant params.
- Workloads: synthetic streaming traces and recorded production traces (sanitized) to reproduce prefix-heavy long-context patterns; sequences up to 32k tokens to exercise KV cache.
- Measurements: cold-start (no cache, cold allocator), warm-start (hot KV cache, warmed with 5 sequences), continuous-batching: variable batching windows (10/25/50/100ms) using our runtime's continuous batching controller.
- Metrics: tokens/sec, p50/p90/p95/p99 latency per response, tail-latency breakdown (kernel queueing, kernel exec, memcpy, CUDA context setup), memory footprint, GPU utilization, effective batch composition distribution.
notes:
- Avoid conflating quantization accuracy loss with different compilation kernels; repeat critical cells with kernel-pin flags.
- Use deterministic seeds for calibration runs.
- For INT8, include both symmetric and asymmetric quant tables to understand outlier sensitivity.
- Instrument the runtime to emit KV-cache hit/miss and cached-prefix-length histograms for each request.
- Schedule runs to avoid node-level interference; isolate experiments to dedicated instances.

final_notes: This ticket aims to make quantized profile adoption an evidence-driven decision: pairing raw throughput wins with clear operational parameters (batch window, warm-up strategy) and concrete accuracy checks. The memo should guide runtime defaults and Console UX for 'recommended profiles'.
